source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Classes and Objects
content: A class is a Java blueprint that defines fields and methods. It describes what objects of that type can store and do.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Classes and Objects
content: An object is a runtime instance created from a class. The expression Student s = new Student(); creates an object and stores a reference.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Classes and Objects
content: A constructor initializes object state when Java creates an instance. Constructors have the same name as the class and no return type.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Classes and Objects
content: Instance fields belong to each object. Static members belong to the class itself and are shared rather than copied per object.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: Encapsulation keeps object state behind a clear boundary. Private fields and public methods work together to control access.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: A getter can expose read access to private state without allowing outside code to directly mutate the field.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: A setter can validate input before changing a private field, so the object protects its own invariants.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: Encapsulation is not perfect security. It is a design practice for reducing accidental misuse and making code easier to maintain.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: Inheritance models an is-a relationship. In Java, a subclass uses extends to inherit accessible behavior from a superclass.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: A subclass can add fields or methods while reusing behavior from its parent class.
keywords: subclass parent reuse behavior fields methods

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: Inheritance should not be used only because two classes share code. If the relationship is has-a, composition is usually clearer.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Encapsulation and Inheritance
content: A child class does not inherit private fields as directly accessible members, but it can use public or protected behavior provided by the parent.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Method overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists. Java resolves the call using the method signature.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Changing only a return type does not overload a Java method. The parameter list must differ.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Overloading is commonly used for convenience, such as print(int value) and print(String value).

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Overloaded method selection happens from compile-time information, not from runtime subclass dispatch.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides a compatible replacement for a superclass method.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: The @Override annotation helps Java detect whether a method truly overrides a parent method.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: To override, the method name and compatible parameter signature must match the superclass method.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Overriding supports specialized subclass behavior while preserving a common method contract.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Polymorphism lets one reference type work with different object types that share a parent type or interface.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: When a parent reference points to a child object, Java uses the actual object type to choose an overridden method at runtime.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Dynamic dispatch is the runtime mechanism that makes overriding behave polymorphically.

source_title: Java OOP Foundations: Overloading Overriding and Polymorphism
content: Polymorphism helps code depend on common behavior while allowing each subclass to respond in its own way.
